scope: Static candidate trace following a Split-related call on a retained runtime-derived analysis image. No native Split command was executed.
observations: The retained decompilation of 0x14067cec0 calls 0x14033bc70 after a successful 0x14032a500 and passes its return to 0x14034aba0.

Candidate 0x14033bc70 allocates one container, labels records and invokes 0x14033b7c0 from each initially unlabelled record. The latter traverses up to three non-null linked records and propagates the label subject to flags.

Candidate 0x14033bc70 invokes 0x14033ba20 once per label with the same allocated container. Candidate 0x14033ba20 marks referenced records and appends selected records and triples into that container.
Candidate 0x14034aba0 replaces one pointer field and updates apparent back-pointers.
interpretation: The static structure is consistent with labelling connected face regions, copying them into a single mesh-like container and attaching it to the existing object. This interpretation is tentative; field types, object identity and visible result semantics are inferred.

provenance.independentDecode: Ghidra instruction starts were decoded with Capstone. All 108, 19 and 161 starts of candidates 0x14033bc70, 0x14034aba0 and 0x14033ba20 had matching mnemonics. Candidate 0x14033b7c0 had 172 starts, with one cmovz/cmove mnemonic alias difference; operands, function boundaries and semantic types were not independently verified.
provenance.resourceGuard: Both static analyses ran separately under a 4 GiB job guard with cleanup confirmed.

limitations: The entry point and branches have not been demonstrated reachable from an actual native Split operation.
No native input, output, object count, GUI state, ownership, or save/reopen behavior was observed.
This evidence alone does not resolve the folded-cutter and disjoint-source part-count mismatches.
